title: Constructibility of semistable and stable geometric fibre conditions
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $\eta$ be its generic point, and let $(X,D)$ and $(Y,E)$ be multipointed $S$-curves [def-trf-multipointed-curve]: the structural maps of each pair are flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$, and the marking is a closed immersion. Let $f_X:Y\to X$, $f_D:E\to D$ be proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] commuting with the markings. Assume that both maps are isomorphisms on the generic fibre and over schematically dense open subsets of their respective targets; an open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense if $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_W$ is injective. For $s\in S$, take a geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] over an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$. Call $s$ semistable if each singular point of $Y_\Omega$ has completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $E_s$ is etale over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $E_s$ lies in the smooth locus of $Y_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Call $s$ stable if it is semistable and no irreducible component of $Y_\Omega$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$, contracted by $(f_X)_\Omega$, and meets the union of $E_\Omega$ and the singular points of $Y_\Omega$ in at most two points. Then both the semistable set and the stable set are constructible subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset] of $S$. No semistability hypothesis on all of $(Y,E)$, and no generization stability of either set, is imposed or asserted.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii) and its proof, printed p. 34: constructibility of the semistable-fibre set and of the subset with no exceptional geometric components; no generization assertion.

proof.text: Write $p:Y\to S$, $q:E\to S$ and $i:E\hookrightarrow Y$ for the structure and marking maps. The schemes $Y$ and $E$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since both structure maps are finitely presented and hence of finite type. The closed-subset minimality theorem [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] gives the Noetherian topological property for $Y,E$ and $S$. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-open-locus] to $p$. It gives an open $U\subseteq Y$ with closed complement $B_Y$. For every $s\in S$, $Y_s\cap B_Y$ is empty exactly when the chosen geometric fibre $Y_\Omega$ has only ordinary nodes as singularities. The fibre criterion in that lemma applies to the given flat finitely presented pure-dimensional curve; it includes smooth fibres.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion of the openness, Chevalley and weighted component-data argument. Primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq E$ be the union of all open neighbourhoods on which $q$ is etale, and let $W\subseteq Y$ be the union of all open neighbourhoods on which $p$ is smooth. These are open by their definitions as unions. Put $B_E=(E\setminus V)\cup i^{-1}(Y\setminus W)$, a closed subset of $E$. The equivalence in [lem-sbc-flat-fibre-etale-neighbourhoods], applied to the flat locally finitely presented map $q$, says that $E_s$ is etale precisely when its fibre avoids $E\setminus V$. The pointwise equivalence in [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion], applied to the flat locally finitely presented map $p$, says that $i(E_s)$ lies in the smooth locus of $Y_s$ precisely when $E_s$ avoids $i^{-1}(Y\setminus W)$. Consequently the two marking conditions hold together exactly when $E_s\cap B_E=\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion of the openness, Chevalley and weighted component-data argument. Primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The closed subsets $B_Y\subseteq Y$ and $B_E\subseteq E$ are constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset], since $Y,E$ are Noetherian. Both $p$ and $q$ are quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and the Noetherian base $S$ is quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] separately to these two maps and closed subsets. Their images are constructible. By steps 1--2 the semistable set is exactly $C=S\setminus(p(B_Y)\cup q(B_E))$. It is constructible by the Boolean-algebra assertion in [def-weil-constructible-subset]. This takes an image of bad points, without assuming either structural curve map proper.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion of the openness, Chevalley and weighted component-data argument. Primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $C$ as a finite union of locally closed subsets using [def-weil-constructible-subset]. On each such subset take the reduced induced closed subscheme of a containing open of $S$, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; call it $T$. These schemes are Noetherian: an immersion is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft], every inverse image of an affine open of $S$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] because the immersion identifies it with a subset of $S$, and hence the immersion is of finite type over $S$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies. Pull back both multipointed pairs to $T$, and later to every reduced closed subscheme of $T$. They remain multipointed by the first clause of [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change], and their two maps remain proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The geometric fibres, including their markings and maps, are the original fibres: open restrictions and radical quotients do not change residue fields. Every fibre of the source pair over these bases is thus semistable. We do not assert that the pulled-back maps remain modifications.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion of the openness, Chevalley and weighted component-data argument. Primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For each $T$ of step 4, prove by Noetherian induction the following claim: every closed subset $Z\subseteq T$ admits a finite partition into locally closed subsets on each of which the contracted-component multiset $(p_R,a_R,b_R)$ is constant. Induction is valid by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]; the empty set has the empty partition. Give $Z$ and its irreducible components their reduced induced structures using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There are finitely many components by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]. On each component apply [lem-trf-contracted-component-generic-data]; all hypotheses hold by step 4, and a reduced irreducible component is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Shrink its nonempty open further by deleting its intersections with the other components. The resulting opens are disjoint, and their union $O$ is open dense in $Z$: its complement is the finite union of the componentwise closed complements. On each open the multiset is constant. The closed subset $Z\setminus O$ is strictly smaller when $Z\ne\varnothing$, so the induction hypothesis partitions it. Adding the finitely many chosen opens proves the claim. Taking $Z=T$ gives a finite partition of $T$ into loci with constant multiset.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion of the openness, Chevalley and weighted component-data argument. Primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix one of the geometric fibres and a contracted reduced irreducible component $R$. It is proper by [lem-trf-contracted-component-generic-data]. The component-geometry assertion of [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction] says that the only singularities of $R$ are its self-nodes. Thus $a_R=0$ is equivalent to $R$ being smooth; intersections with other components cause no singularity on $R$ itself. If also $p_R=0$, the smooth proper connected curve $R$ has genus zero and [lem-trf-genus-zero-smooth-proper-line] gives $R\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. Conversely, if $R\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$, then [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero] gives smoothness and $H^1(R,\mathcal O_R)=0$, so $a_R=p_R=0$. By the definition of $b_R$, this component is exceptional in the precise sense of the item if and only if its triple has $p_R=0$, $a_R=0$ and $b_R\leq2$. In particular, a self-node is counted once in $b_R$, rather than twice as branches, and is separately detected by $a_R$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion of the openness, Chevalley and weighted component-data argument. Primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: On each piece of the finite partitions from step 5, the existence of a triple $(0,0,b)$ with $b\leq2$ is constant. Step 6 identifies this with the existence of an exceptional component. The stable subset of each $T$ is therefore the union of just those pieces on which no such triple occurs. Each piece is locally closed in $T$, hence in $S$, and there are finitely many pieces over the finitely many initial $T$. By [def-weil-constructible-subset], their selected union is constructible in the Noetherian scheme $S$. It equals the stable set because all these $T$ lie in the semistable set $C$ and cover $C$. Together with step 3 this proves both assertions. No stability under generization is used.

lean.statement: theorem stable_modification_constructibility {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral S] [IsNoetherian S] (η : S) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) (X Y : MultipointedCurve S) (f : Y.Hom X) (hf : f.IsEtaModification (S.fromSpecResidueField η)) : ∃ Cₛ Cₜ : Set S, Topology.IsConstructible Cₛ ∧ Topology.IsConstructible Cₜ ∧ (∀ s : S, s ∈ Cₛ ↔ ((MultipointedPair.ofCurve Y).baseChange (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).IsSemistable) ∧ (∀ s : S, s ∈ Cₜ ↔ ((MultipointedPair.ofCurve Y).baseChange (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).IsSemistable ∧ MultipointedPair.HasGeometricStability ((MultipointedPair.ofCurve Y).baseChange (S.fromSpecResidueField s)) ((MultipointedPair.ofCurve X).baseChange (S.fromSpecResidueField s)) ((Over.pullback (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk Y.x) (V := Over.mk X.x) f.curve f.curve_over)))
